question.text: Under the SSE framework, the offer documents of social enterprises for various modes of fundraising shall require disclosure of aspects called _________.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 3.3.1 and Table 3.2 explicitly use the term 'Differentiators'. These 11 heads — Vision, Target Segment, Strategy, Governance, Management, Operations, Finance, Compliance, Credibility, Social Impact, Risks — help funders differentiate between similar NPOs/SEs and make informed investment decisions. This is also reproduced verbatim in Sample Q4 of the chapter. The Trap: KPIs and Risk Factors exist as sub-concepts within Differentiators (Risk is Row 11; Social Impact is Row 10 which contains KPIs). Basis of Allotment is a public-issue allotment term, not a disclosure head. Candidates must remember the specific SEBI-coined term. Cross-Exam Context: XII (SMF) introduces offer documents generally. III-A compliance covers prospectus disclosures under Main Board ICDR. XV (RA) reads offer documents but doesn't term them 'differentiators' — that is SSE-specific nomenclature under ICDR Chapter X-A. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Map each of the 11 differentiators to evidence sources BEFORE the offer-document review: Vision (constitution/MoA), Governance (board minutes & Form 2), Finance (audited FS), Social Impact (past SAS reports / programme logs). If any row is unsupported, draft a qualified assurance statement rather than a clean one.
